Role: Marketing Coordinator
Industry: Education Management
Company size: 5,001-10,000 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Kanban boards have helped me organize mail campaigns, content for social networks, and digital advertising in general. I divide projects into progression lists so I can organize our resources according to what I need: time, money and staff. The integration with other external software is just wonderful: Slack for real-time communications and notifications, Google Drive for storage, Mailchimp for automatic campaigns, etc. Also, customizable templates save us a lot of time. And Butler simplifies repetitive tasks that I don't want to do. It's like a virtual secretary.
Cons: I know Trello is designed to be extremely simple, but I would like to be able to employ statistics to evaluate ROI.
Comments: In marketing, we require many types of employees to move a project forwards. Trello helps me communicate and manage tasks that need [truncated]

Cons: Less user friendly than other programs. Layout is clean but could be improved in functionality. It was a great initial program when going to an online workflow organization format but not the best fit for my specific needs.
Comments: Overall it was a good experience. While it wasn't the best fit for me, it is a great option when looking at workflow management tools.

Role: Brand Designer
Industry: Design
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: If you love organising your projects from a visual place this software is my favourite to use. I really that I can lay it out in an editorial fashion and include instructions and ideas in the cards. Trello also gives you some prompts that work for the project you're working on at the time. I've used it for designing websites and magazine layouts to organizing a course structure.
Cons: For tasks it seems to really hit the mark, but you cannot create roadmaps. It also doesn't offer analytics or any reporting. There's a lot of paid add-ons which can extend your capabilities to level up project management options but they will add up.
Comments: It's an intuitive project management tool for small teams that want a simply no frills way to track tasks. People who haven't great technical skills will find it easy to navigate.

Role: Small Business Owner
Industry: Consumer Services
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: ClickUp is one of the best tools on the market today. Their variety of templates available is incredible. My team and I use this tool for project management and CRM needs. They have a variety of plans to fit a variety of needs - from the free forever plan to a small teams plan priced at $7/user, a mid-size team plan priced at $12/user and an enterprise team plan. The available features on the free forever plan alone are incredible and include the ability to use unlimited tasks, have unlimited plan members, use whiteboards, enjoy real-time chat, and use many different views. Also included in the free forever plan is 24-7 support. I'm not aware of any other tool that has such a robust feature offering for a free plan. It's served my team and I very well with our PM & CRM needs at no additional cost. As a small business with a carefully [truncated]

Role: Sr. Accounting manager
Industry: Accounting
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5

Pros: Click up keeps our team tasks very organized. You can categorize types of tasks, status and cadence of each task. It also has time tracking for each task which is a huge plus. Great for team collaboration and managing all tasks.
Cons: There is nothing that I do not like about click up as it is very user friendly and intuitive.

Role: Process Manager
Industry: Machinery
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: ClickUp gives you so many ways to view and manage your projects—List, Kanban, Calendar, Gantt Chart, Timeline, and even more. It’s rare to find a tool that caters to so many different working styles. Also everything from task statuses to custom fields can be tailored. Whether you’re running a simple to-do list or a complex product launch with dependencies, ClickUp can be shaped to fit your needs. It feels like a tool that grows with you, no matter how sophisticated your workflows get.
Cons: ClickUp does so much that it can feel overwhelming at first. When I started using it, I spent a good chunk of time just figuring out what all the features did. It’s worth it, but if you’re someone who needs a tool that’s simple out of the box, you might feel frustrated.
Comments: ClickUp does almost everything, and it does most of it well. I like how [truncated]
